USE CASES

Memory for systems where
evidence and scope matter.

These are realistic evaluation targets derived from the current architecture. They are not customer, compliance, or production-deployment claims.

01

Agent memory

Problem
Long-running agents need to update and retrieve context without turning every prior interaction into an unscoped text pile.
MESA role
MESA provides a durable mutation lifecycle, dataset-scoped sessions, structured assertions, and observable outcomes.
Expected benefit
A clearer basis for inspecting what was remembered, from which source, and under which scope.
02

Knowledge-heavy assistants

Problem
A single similarity score can miss exact wording, explicit relationships, and multi-hop context.
MESA role
MESA fuses vector, BM25, assertion, and bounded graph-path origins around canonical evidence.
Expected benefit
Broader retrieval signals without discarding evidence identity or treating graph projection as canonical truth.
03

Provenance-sensitive AI

Problem
Returned context may be useful but impossible to trace back to a document revision, chunk, or span.
MESA role
Source and pipeline provenance remain part of the V4 assertion and retrieval contracts.
Expected benefit
Applications can surface the basis and limitations of retrieved context.
04

Long-lived structured memory

Problem
Facts change, sources are revised, and shared artifacts may have more than one owner.
MESA role
V4 models immutable revisions, supersession, source-owned rollback, purge, replay, and reconciliation.
Expected benefit
Memory can evolve through explicit lifecycle rules instead of silent replacement.

CURRENT VERTICAL EXAMPLE

MESA Law explores
the legal workflow shape.

Its source-aware matter, document, review, and QA surfaces show why provenance matters. Live Core integration remains pending.
